newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SPADEL SAYS PORTUGUESE UNIT BANKRUPT.
newsitem.headline: SPADEL SAYS PORTUGUESE UNIT BANKRUPT.

text.p: Belgian mineral water group Spadel said in a statement on Tuesday its Portuguese unit Empresa Das Aguas Do Alardo decided to file for bankruptcy.

"After the regrettable events that blocked the industrial and commercial activities of Alardo during two weeks in March this year, it had become clear that disproportionate means would be needed to relaunch activities to recapture volume and market share," Spadel said in a statement.

Alardo was shut down on March 10 by Portuguese authorities after bottles of its water were found to contain traces of algae. Production and sales restarted March 20 after further tests revealed the water was safe for consumption.
Spadel said efforts to sell Alardo had been fruitless.
Spadel said the bankruptcy's impact on its 1997 accounts would be limited after most of its Alardo investment was written off in its 1996 book year.
The company would decide later in the year how to provision about 80 million francs in outstanding loans and guarantees to Alardo.
